anuttara_01: In this highest state of supreme God consciousness there is no need of spiritual progress, no contemplation, no art of expression, no investigation, no meditation, no concentration, no recitation, exertion or practice. Tell me then, what is the supreme and well-ascertained truth? Listen indeed to this! Neither abandon nor accept anything, enjoy everything. Remain as you are!
anuttara_02: In reality, there is no such thing as birth and death, so how can the question arise of bondage for living beings? There never was any such bondage for the one who is entirely free, and therefore, to struggle for liberation is useless and nothing more than delusion — like a dark shadow mistaken for a demon, or a rope seen as a snake. Neither abandon nor accept anything, remain as you are, well established in your own Self.
anuttara_03: In the oneness of that supreme state of anuttara, what talk can there be, and what differentiated path of adorer, adored and adoration? Wonder of wonders! Though it appears differentiated, this illusion is no other than consciousness, one without a second. Everything is nothing but the pure essence of your own Self-experience, so why worry in vain?
anuttara_04: One cannot compare the bliss of this state to the intoxication of wealth or wine, nor to the union with a beloved woman. This excessive joy of the Self is comparable only to the weight of that blissful state which descends when one gets liberated from all differentiation. The flow of this supreme consciousness is nothing other than your own treasure abode that you had temporarily forgotten.
anuttara_05: Attraction and repulsion, pleasure and pain, rising and setting, self-confidence and depression; all these states with which the universe is formed shine as mutually different but in reality, they are not. Whenever you perceive the specificity of some thing, at that very moment perceive the essence of your own consciousness as one with it — why not take delight in the fullness of that awareness?
anuttara_06: In this world the totality of objects appear eternally in the present moment. Differentiated action is an illusion based on the unlawful pervasion of an intermediate state which is unreal, transient, fraudulent, just a heap of appearances like the illusion of a dream. Remain above these defects forged by doubt — be awakened!
anuttara_07: For the insentient there is no outflow of objective things, for those are manifested only when experienced by thee. Though deprived of reality they share reality in one instant through erroneous perception. Thus the greatness of this universe arises from your own imagination — it does not take birth from anything else. Therefore you alone shine in all these worlds, and though one, you become many by your own glory!
anuttara_08: Real or unreal, small or plentiful, eternal or momentary — this universe rising from your own consciousness and becoming one with your essence appears glorified in the mirror of Consciousness. Having ascertained the sublimity of the universe, enjoy universal sovereignty.
bhairava_01: Great God, pervading all moving and unmoving things, pure spirit, one, eternal, infinite, refuge of the helpless — with my mind filled with Thee, I worship Thee in my loving heart.
bhairava_02: By the energy of your grace it has been revealed to me that this vibrating universe is your own existence. O Lord Shiva, you are my own soul, and as such this universe is my own expression and existence.
bhairava_03: O possessor of everything, though your devotees are caught in the net of destiny that arouses troubles and bondage, still they are not afraid of the fret and fever of this world. Fear exists only when there is someone else to inflict it — but when there is none other than You, how can fear arise?
bhairava_04: O angel of death, do not look towards me with wrathful and frightening eyes, for I am always absorbed in the worship of Lord Shiva. One with the energy of the terrifying Bhairava, your dreadful looks can do me no harm.
bhairava_05: O Lord Bhairava, I offer salutations to you who has awakened me to the realization that everything in existence is you alone. The darkness of my mind destroyed, I fear neither the demons of karma nor Yama, the Lord of death.
bhairava_06: O Lord Shiva, through real knowledge I realize all attachments and all that exists is activated by you. My mind saturated with immortal devotion, I experience supreme bliss.
bhairava_07: O Lord, sometimes misery torments my mind, but at that same moment, blessed by a shower of your grace, a clear vision of my oneness with you arises, and my mind feels appeased.
bhairava_08: O Lord Shiva, charity, ritual bath and penance subside worldly troubles — but even more, remembrance of your sacred words pours a stream of peace into my heart.
bhairava_09: O Lord Bhairava, through my utmost faith I have perceived you in the unique sacrifice of oneness. Filled with your presence, my consciousness dances and sings, enjoying its own ecstasy.
bhairava_10_phala: I, Abhinavagupta, composed this hymn on the tenth of the dark fortnight of Pausha. By its meditation and recitation, merciful Lord Bhairava swiftly destroys the torments of this wilderness of worldly existence.
bpc_01: He is one, within and without, the unfailing form of all lights and darknesses; both radiance and darkness are His.
bpc_02: He alone is the Supreme Lord, the very nature of all beings; all that arises is His power, steeped in lordship.
bpc_03: Power does not seek separation from the Possessor of power; their oneness is eternal, like fire and fuel.
bpc_04: He alone is Bhairava, God, whose nature is sustaining the world; all reflected by His power resembles His own Self.
bpc_05: His supreme Goddess yearns to touch His own form; in all existences His fullness is neither less nor more.
bpc_06: This God, united with this Goddess, ever eager for divine play, simultaneously creates and destroys the manifold universe, being all-powerful.
bpc_07: That He accomplishes what seems most difficult is His unsurpassed freedom: this is sovereignty, lordship, and the very form of consciousness.
bpc_08: Limited brightness is the mark of the inert; consciousness differs from inertia because it cannot be measured or bounded.
bpc_09: Thus, for the independent One who enjoys His own power, creation and dissolution abide as His very nature.
bpc_10: In them is endless variety: upward, downward, across; worlds, their parts, and the extremes of pleasure and pain.
bpc_11: Full knowledge of this is called freedom; for the deluded, that very thing is the fearsome samsara.
bpc_12: It comes from the essence of His grace, from guru, Agama, or any scripture of the Supreme Lord, from whatever source.
bpc_13: Knowledge of that reality is liberation from the Supreme Lord; for the awakened, its fullness is known as living freedom.
bpc_14: Bondage and liberation are not divided from the form of the Supreme Lord; in truth, no distinction exists in Him.
bpc_15: Thus Bhairava, resting on the lotus-trident of will, creativity, knowledge, and power, is contemplated as the nature of all beings.
dhs_01: The body is called God's temple; the Self is the eternal deity. Cast off ignorance's garland and worship Him with the feeling 'I am He.'
dhs_02: I salute Ganapati, praised by hosts of demons and gods, ever intent on granting desired boons, the best of all sights, worthy of worship, whose body is life.
dhs_03: I salute the youthful Bhairava named Apana, whose feet are worshipped by hosts of heroic yoginis and streams of siddhas, who removes the suffering of the humble.
dhs_04: By whose power the world shines to devotees as Shiva's path, I always salute that stainless true Guru, whose form is attention.
dhs_05: I salute that consciousness-filled Bliss-Bhairava, whom the goddesses of the senses ever worship in the heart-lotus with their enjoyments of sense objects.
dhs_06: I salute that Bliss-Bhairavi, whose form is reflective awareness, who ceaselessly plays at the world's arising, manifestation, and devouring.
dhs_07: I constantly bow to that Brahmani, whose form is intellect, who, stationed on the petal of the Lord of Gods, worships Bhairava with flowers of resolve.
dhs_08: I salute that Shambhavi Mother, whose form is ego, who, stationed on fire's petal, ever worships Bhairava with flowers of pride.
dhs_09: I salute that Kaumari, whose form is mind, who, moving on the southern petal, ever worships Bhairava with flowers of distinction.
dhs_10: I constantly bow to that Vaishnavi Power, whose form is revelation, who, moving on the southwest petal, worships Bhairava with flowers of sound.
dhs_11: I bow to Varahi, stationed in the western mandala, skin-clad, pleasing Bhairava with heart-stealing flowers of touch.
dhs_12: I praise Indrani, embodiment of sight, seated in the wind-direction mandala, of surpassing form, who worships Bhairava.
dhs_13: I bow to Chamunda, called Tongue, dwelling in the Lord of Wealth's lotus, ever worshipping Bhairava with diverse six-flavored foods.
dhs_14: I ever bow to Mahalakshmi, called Smell, seated in Isha's lotus, who worships Bhairava with manifold fragrances.
dhs_15: I praise the ever-giver of accomplishments, called Self, Lord of the Field, worshipped in six systems, enfolded by thirty-six tattvas.
dhs_16: I bow to the wheel of presiding deities of one's own body, ever arising thus, essence of pulsing experience, constantly present within all.
stc_001: Through sweet, mind-stealing speech, through Paśyantī, through manifestation, the Supreme Lord's blissful majesty triumphs.
stc_002: Expanded by the wealth of gracious compassion-awareness and supreme bliss, His greatness lit by knowledge, the Unconquered One triumphs.
stc_003: Salutations to the infinite Light, ocean of Śaṅkara's milk, whose Self is pure nectar, spreading as point and sound.
stc_004: We hate You, we praise You; we chant to You, O Lord of Ambika. Very attainable, You have well sustained our world.
stc_005: Salutations to Śambhu, the Lord who is withdrawn-contact union, born of perfect nectar, and all-pervading Māyā in nature.
stc_006: We salute Pārameśvara, the universal form undivided in divisions and uncut in all that can be severed.
stc_007: Salutations to the Immovable, smaller than Om's half-mātrā yet vast, whose quality is attributelessness beyond the cosmic egg.
stc_008: We praise the Swan-Power of the Lord-Swan who pervades space and moves everywhere, carrying the cosmic egg in her womb.
stc_009: Without any material support He alone paints the world-picture on the wall; salutations to the Trident-bearer, glory of the arts.
stc_010: O Hara-Hamsa, grant us here Śiva's self-milked knowledge, purified after being drawn from Māyā's web-womb.
stc_011: We offer ourselves to You, the Existing One, the one reality of ultimate truth, undivided amid distinctions delimited by the six means of valid knowledge.
stc_012: May we behold Your deep, lovely cave, free of darkness, encircled by supreme light, and enter within.
stc_013: Salutations even to those who, even in dream, behold the Lord with moon-digit-adorned crest, giver of supreme bliss.
stc_014: O Lord, the taste for cultivating the state of being, skilled in cutting rebirth's fear, pleases all; whom does it not delight?
stc_015: O Lord of the world, as long as life lasts, may this be our duty: by Your grace, to abide with one-pointed mind on You.
stc_016: Homage to Śambhu, whose being is the Vedas and Āgamas spreading in a thousand branches, the wish-fulfilling tree yielding endless fruits.
stc_017: O Lord, applying speech, mind, and bodily acts to You, may we become imbued with You, free from duality, somewhere, somehow.
stc_018: Homage to the Trident-bearer, endowed with independent power in the reality-grounded ordering of worlds' creation and dissolution.
stc_019: Let even the name of the great Matted One beyond qualities, chief object of meditation, be contemplated—what fruit from other supports?
stc_020: Praiseworthy are those who rely on the power of the mantra 'Namo Namaḥ Śivāya' and strive to enjoy Śāmbhava splendour.
stc_021: O Lord, what path fails to reach You, what speech fails to speak You, what meditation fails to contemplate You—what exists that You are not?
stc_022: May this essence—'He is worshipped, meditated upon, and pleased'—flow in a thousand streams and increase in me toward You.
stc_023: Homage to You, Lord, Immovable Pillar, wearing a serpent as sacred thread, whose Self is the abode of the garland of all leaves of wisdom.
stc_024: O Bhava, Your remembrance is the one medicine for ignorance's darkness; by granting this and that, may Your grace work in me.
stc_025: Salutations to Īśa, fulfiller of every human aim; even the obeisance of the wise here is fitly offered to Him.
stc_026: Drowned in the fearful ocean of saṃsāra, the home of sorrows, those who attain Śarva, the jewel of devotees' hopes, conquer all.
stc_027: O Dhūrjaṭa, You are known to those whose treasure is unobscured, non-dual, steadfast knowledge; who indeed are these that know You?
stc_028: Though without qualities, He is the sole object of the knowledge of guṇas; the Unborn triumphs. Though desireless by nature, He is the highest fruit of desires.
stc_029: O Vibho, the milky ocean of majesty, not won by gods' striving for fortune's jewel-nectar, is naturally Yours alone.
stc_030: With devotion I bow for humanity's liberation; O Bhava, protect them; to Śambhu, auspicious and fearless, giver of remembrance and dance.
stc_031: All-knowing, all-doing, You are all—so say the wise. What is knowable or doable, Lord, that is not offered by You to the Infinite?
stc_032: Your will alone bears the fruit of the three worlds—O Lord, who knows how far Your works extend?
stc_033: Even Brahmā and others ascend again and again on the stairway of His deeds to reach His abode; I bow to Him.
stc_034: This Brahmā, this Mahendra, these two, sun and moon—thus the vine of His power blossoms; may that Bhava protect us.
stc_035: Even deluded minds cannot bring him error; his end is hard for far-goers, yet he is gentle to the praiser.
stc_036: Salutations in praise, remembrance, meditation, sight, touch, and attainment to the mass of bliss, compassionate, matted-haired.
stc_037: O Lord, even when my mind asks, 'What is this delight?', by delight I am yours; not in myself—what joy!
stc_038: Though I ponder countless duties and my mind is fickle, resting beyond being and nonbeing, may I delight greatly in bliss.
stc_039: O Lord, if your subtle form is only a fraction of the three worlds, how could your gross form fail to charm even Brahma and the rest?
stc_040: O God, if you alone were not what these words express, what anguish would the wise endure in the net of speech!
stc_041: O Lord, by what sequence, act, or insight may the teaching 'You are visible' bring grace to me?
stc_042: Salutations to the matted-haired one, without motive, sole benefactor of the three worlds, desired by all yet free from desire.
stc_043: Ah, this knowledge of the field serves the great aim of the good: by it they plant in you, O Lord, devotion of endless fruit.
stc_044: O Enchanter, how vast is your illusion! Even after gaining the treasure of meditating on you, the deluded world grows lax.
stc_045: At the outset, be everywhere, whether as act or instrument; let the world exist, yet You alone are its free doer.
stc_046: Who but You has the power or compassion to lift the three worlds, seized by the duality of the three qualities and three vibrations?
stc_047: O God, what fault is a fault resolved to attain You? What merit is merit resolved not to attain You?
stc_048: O God, great is this act of meditating on You; in it, who from Brahma down is not qualified for our liberation?
stc_049: The start of every undertaking, the finish of every act, and the varied thoughts between: O Lord, these lie on the path of Your mind.
stc_050: O Lord, no higher expansion of joys, thousandfold richer, is seen anywhere except in the nectar of devotion to You.
stc_051: Homage to Lord Soma, moon-adorned, who gathers desire and stretches its range.
stc_052: Powerless and without resolve everywhere, what can I do? The all-gracious Shakti, Shankari, is my refuge.
stc_053: O Lord, beyond qualities, whose Self is defined as complete transcendence, in what part is Your supreme reflection found?
stc_054: O Lord, though You are the non-dual, conditionless Self, even now Your measurable maya deceives us.
stc_055: O Bhava, attainment of powers, eternal sovereignty, and end of becoming are the tender leaves on the wish-fulfilling tree of devotion to You.
stc_056: Here, every direction is soaked in worldly time. Even having gained this, when will you reach its end, O Lord? Tell me.
stc_057: I bow to Śambhu, the Great Swan, sole dweller in the peaceful, virtuous mind, radiant with abundant glory.
stc_058: May the lamp of awakening to You be mine, O Lord, the lamp of devotion burning the heart's proud darkness and all the fuel of saṃsāra.
stc_059: Who but You, O Hara, is the poet able to project and reabsorb the three-world drama, teeming with countless seeds of existence?
stc_060: I bow to the Free and the Bound, who can turn being into non-being or non-being into being, sole master of dissolution and lordship.
stc_061: Whatever joy appears even within the three worlds is only a drop of Him; I salute that God, the ocean of bliss.
stc_062: Ah, blessed are Brahmā and the rest who, liberated, chant the glorious tale 'Obeisance to Śiva,' overcome with joy.
stc_063: Salutations to You, O Bhava: though desireless, You create endless desires; though beginningless, You enjoy the universe.
stc_064: We seek no benefit in praising the Lord, primal root of the three worlds' beginning, since He is perfect dharma.
stc_065: Even great, excellent purpose-fulfillers are stained by delusion’s mass; remembering Him, minds grow clear; praise auspicious Śiva.
stc_066: O Lord, Your sovereign power here is inviolate; by Your will alone the three worlds dissolve and arise.
stc_067: Even evil offered to You becomes supreme merit, O Lord; since You are nowhere else, even merit finds its worth in You.
stc_068: Seizing Him in the fist, they cry, ‘We have seen You; where will You flee?’ Though devotion is beyond attainment, the blessed hasten to Śiva.
stc_069: We praise You, beyond the purest essence of Rig, Yajur, and Saman; O profound, beautiful One, You are the Vedas’ knowable Self.
stc_070: O Paramēśvara, You are the Ordainer, beginning and end of the universe; if not from You, whence could the host of dharma arise?
stc_071: Salutations to You, O God: You raise and shatter the world’s bewildering delusion; veiling non-dual knowledge-bliss, You reveal it.
stc_072: To whom could finite distinctions be offered by any wish? May Śiva, catching Māyā in one blink, guard us from it.
stc_073: O Lord of lords, You uphold the sublime path of dispassion, the supreme radiance of knowledge, and the utmost summit of desirelessness.
stc_074: You are Brahman even to Brahmā; O Ruler, whose lord are You not? Who knows how far You are the blessing of the world’s blessings?
stc_075: What need of other kin, friends, or masters? Everywhere, O my Lord, You are the rescuer from the ocean of existence.
stc_076: Victorious are those who can wash away stains of delusion and māyā, drawn by Śaiva yoga's power and sprinkled with divine nectar.
stc_077: May the Lord whose brilliance the Gāyatrī sings, inspiring all minds, inspire our minds onto the good path.
stc_078: O Eight-formed Lord, will You not give us eternal stability in even one form? If pleased, You will do all.
stc_079: The truth of things generally produces meaningful action; from You, O Lord, even Your name grants fulfillment unto liberation.
stc_080: By Your power that repeatedly conceives each varied state of this wondrous world, Lord, what wise person is not amazed?
stc_081: We remember Cupid's foe, whose one heroic remembrance makes difficult things easy and sorrow joyful.
stc_082: Victorious are songs whose theme is the Supreme Lord, by whose name even great souls bristle with joyful rapture.
stc_083: If supreme being is just as You are, You are the withdrawal of the threefold world's beginning, spread by Your own power's array.
stc_084: You are mantra, worthy of mantra, and its master; apart from You there is none. Grant me that mantra, Lord, that I may become Your mantra.
stc_085: O Lord, You are Being itself, true resolve, the Self I too am; what is this saṃsāra, this dream in You?
stc_086: That indestructible, inaccessible, one, well-founded: O Lord, it is sovereignty for those who offer action’s fruits to You.
stc_087: Able to crush every calamity, to grant or withhold every blessing, that Bull-bannered God of gods is our merciful Lord.
stc_088: The divine eye of knowledge, blinded by māyā’s impurity: Lord, devotion to You is the supreme ointment that cleanses it.
stc_089: Grant me the fearless, blissful, one, imperishable state; come to me swiftly, O God—why do You wait for that?
stc_090: How deep and dreadful by nature is saṃsāra’s ocean; who but supreme Maheśvara is the way across it?
stc_091: I bow to You, end of all completed deeds, destroyer of Madana, Gaṅgā-crowned, who acts rightly for the purpose.
stc_092: For those praying for a state beyond lordship, knowledge, detachment, and duty, O Lord, what highest goal except You?
stc_093: O Śambhu, who does not long for You, though able to bend a straw? Graced by Your will, who would not bear Brāhmī’s burden?
stc_094: Crowned by the jewel of reverence to Hara, unless rich in wisdom, whom would they honor as supreme, whom not honor?
stc_095: O Matted-haired Lord, enthroned amid the ocean of worldly knowledge, You are the still nectar-bestower that frees all delusion.
stc_096: Whatever wonder, whether beheld by strange sight or formed in mind, O Lord, You give as the fully fulfilled fruit of ultimate truth.
stc_097: Who surpasses You in qualities, or who, apart from You, is superior without qualities? O Lord, we bow; mind cannot praise or blame You.
stc_098: Even in Your praise, the nectar-flood yields such fruit of Your grace; who else could drink it, O Lord of worlds - what is there to give?
stc_099: From You, guide and treasury of fulfillment for every worthy aim, O Lord, I pray always to attain only devotion to You.
stc_100: O Lord of the three worlds, salutations to Your power that, for beings delighting in existence, takes on and removes world-lordship.
stc_101: O Master, in doubt over the cause of complete removal of afflictions, having known You are He - who has not gone to You for refuge?
stc_102: Having enjoyed pleasures and abandoned worldly delusion, I shall gain the supreme state; O Shambhu, may this hope be the devotee's highest adornment.
stc_103: O Lord, whatever I do or say, even in dreams, good or bad, with the proud assurance of belonging to You, I am content everywhere.
stc_104: O Lord, Light of lights, for one hastening to Your abode, I deem the mind's touch of darkness a barren woman's child - unreal.
stc_105: He who sets his foot on liberation's path and resolves firmly, 'I shall serve Shiva,' is safe too, I think.
stc_106: Here, in the three worlds' processes of maintenance, arising, and dissolution, You alone, O Lord, are the power of becoming; You behold the sovereign Tantra.
stc_107: Who here in the three worlds is a savior unburned by the three fires? Homage to You, the heart of the nectar of liberation.
stc_108: Even artificial devotion to You yields genuine fruit; if it is wholly sincere, what result? Please tell me.
stc_109: By that gaze You are seen, by that path You are reached; its fruit is unborn, sprung from the wish-fulfilling tree of Your speech.
stc_110: More blessed than blessing is this supreme abiding in You; O Lord, remover of obstacles to it, You are my refuge.
stc_111: Ah, most sweet is the nectar of all service and praise; at each instant, how could it not grow ever new?
stc_112: Who, again and again at rest, yet with hundreds of imaginings, projects the triple world? The one unborn, beyond conception, prevails.
stc_113: O God, when shall I stand before You through knowledge's lamp, burning the filthy oil-wick of samsaric tendencies?
stc_114: O Shambhu, when You set even one moment's step in a fault-free mind, what will You not accomplish?
stc_115: O Lord, may the thought 'I am blessed, my task accomplished, I am great' stand firm for one whose support is You.
stc_116: Though You Yourself are the doer of all good and ill, O Lord, devotion to You alone gives birth to auspiciousness.
stc_117: O Lord, when the mind is glad, why do You enter? People waver, thinking it will become glad by Your entering.
stc_118: Here again the sole certainty is Your sustaining presence; O Lord, the mind's gladness is fulfillment, the supreme state.
stc_119: O Lord, whatever my speech, mind, deed, and body, may they by Your grace become adorned only with devotion to You.
stc_120: O Shambhu, Bhatta Narayana composed this jewel of praise, abundantly granting desire-fruit and sheltering devotion's fortune.
